_schema.research_method: Entry characteristics are drawn from MMT's own agency profiles, org charts and vehicle dataset (in-repo, each dated) and from the 2026-09-20 web search pass recorded in the other data/reference files. Vehicle status is never restated here; read /api/v1/vehicles.
_schema.codes: code matches lib/federal-agencies.js (VA, DHA, CMS, ONC, NIH, CDC, HRSA, IHS, ARPA-H, ASPR, FDA, SAMHSA, AHRQ, HHS, GSA, NASA) plus STATE_MEDICAID for the state segment.
_schema.org_chart_as_of: Taken from each chart page's own as-of statement; null where the page carries none.

buyers.name: Department of Veterans Affairs
entry_characteristics: Enterprise health IT and virtual care for the largest integrated health system in the country; national rollout dynamics across medical centers and VISNs.
Distinct security and accessibility requirements: FedRAMP authorization plus VA's own ATO (VA Notice 25-06), Section 508.
IT services flow through T4NG2 ($60.7B, 33 primes, ordering to March 2036) and SDVOSB-only VECTOR; EHR modernization runs on a single-award Oracle Health IDIQ.
Pathfinder (pathfinder.va.gov) is the vendor front door; every purchase still runs through a VA contracting activity.
watch: CCN Next Gen Medical ($700B ceiling) in source selection since March 2026 (MMT Contract Tracker, 2026-08-17)
SEWP VI ordering opens 2026-11-01 (MMT VA profile, verified 2026-07-09)

buyers.name: Defense Health Agency / Military Health System
entry_characteristics: Enterprise systems (MHS GENESIS in sustainment), deployed and virtual care, records interoperability with VA through FEHRM.

Impact-level sequencing for cloud products: FedRAMP Moderate then IL4 for PHI and CUI, IL5 where the mission owner categorizes the system as NSS or high-sensitivity CUI; CMMC for the contractor's own systems.
Vehicles: Geographic Service Provider (small business, to 2034), PEO DHMS deployment IDIQ (pre-award), OMNIBUS IV for R&D support, Workforce 3.0 in its final ordering year.
Fast doors: the Enterprise-Wide CSO (HT003826SC005) and the MTEC other transaction consortium.

buyers.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
entry_characteristics: Largest HHS IT buyer. Operates its own contract vehicle (SPARC, ordering ends 2027-02-20 with no replacement planned) and its own cloud review path (Rapid Cloud Review for non-FedRAMP SaaS).
Absence of full FedRAMP authorization is not automatically disqualifying at CMS: RCR grants a provisional ATO in about 2 to 3 weeks for low-risk SaaS.
Adjacency to state Medicaid: CMS sets the enhanced-funding conditions, certification (SMC) and interoperability rules (CMS-0057-F) every state system follows.
Innovation Center models (WISeR from 2026-01-01) select technology vendors directly.
watch: Where CMS OIT task orders land after SPARC's ordering period closes 2027-02-20
RMADA 3 awarded July 2026 to 17 companies (MMT Contract Tracker, 2026-08-17)

buyers.name: Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy / Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ASTP/ONC)
entry_characteristics: A standards regulator, not a conventional buyer: certification criteria and interoperability policy shape product requirements across every health buyer.

HTI-4 (effective 2025-10-01) added electronic prior authorization, e-prescribing and real-time prescription benefit criteria; HTI-5 (proposed 2025-12-29) would remove 34 of 60 criteria and is not final.
TEFCA and the information blocking rules are the policy levers that flow into CMS, VA and DoD procurements.
watch: HTI-5 final rule
March 2026 reversal of the ASTP reorganization (MMT org chart, 2026-08-25)

buyers.name: National Institutes of Health (including NITAAC)
entry_characteristics: Research mission framing: program-specific systems, analytics and data platforms; SBIR through the NIH SEED office.

NITAAC is sunsetting: CIO-SP3, CIO-SP3 SB and CIO-CS take no new orders after 2026-10-29; CIO-SP4 was cancelled 2026-01-30; all NITAAC functions cease 2028-12-31. Work moves to GSA (Alliant 3, Polaris, MAS).
An NIH SBIR Phase III is not a reliable purchase route; HHS calls Phase III awards not typical.
watch: 2026-10-29: last day for new NITAAC orders
Where NIH IT services move: GSA vehicles

buyers.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entry_characteristics: Public health mission framing: surveillance, data modernization (OPHDST), analytics and data platforms.
IT operations run through ITOPSS 4.0; OCIO TASS was in market research as of the dataset date.
The 2025 HHS reorganization proposed moving ASPR functions into a CDC Center for Preparedness and Response; Congress requires a plan before CDC functions move.
watch: OCIO TASS: market research to solicitation
Preparedness functions arriving from ASPR if the reorganization proceeds

buyers.name: Health Resources and Services Administration
entry_characteristics: A grant-maker first: health centers, Ryan White, the National Health Service Corps, maternal and child health, 340B. IT and program-support contracting sits behind those programs.

The OPTN Modernization Initiative is the live multi-vendor contracting story: a December 2025 UNOS contract for OPTN operations and the national matching system, and a policy-process support task order to CVP.
Congress's FY2026 Labor-HHS bill rejected folding HRSA into an Administration for a Healthy America; the FY2027 request proposes it again.

buyers.name: Indian Health Service
entry_characteristics: Program-specific systems for tribal and IHS facilities; the PATH EHR modernization IDIQ is in its pilot year (ordering to 2033).
Buy Indian Act set-asides (ISBEE and IEE) run alongside the standard small business programs.
RPMS is the legacy record system being replaced.

buyers.name: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health
entry_characteristics: Innovation funding with published partnering processes: Open BAA, four Mission Office ISOs, Sprints; a different motion from services procurement.
Other transaction authority under 42 U.S.C. 290c; the Director prioritizes work performed in the United States.
FY2027 request $945M, down from $1.5B in FY2026; the STATS IDIQ (shared with NIH) is the one conventional vehicle.

buyers.name: Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (with BARDA)
entry_characteristics: Preparedness funding with published partnering processes: the BARDA BAA on SAM.gov, the DRIVe EZ-BAA for awards under $750,000, other transactions under 42 U.S.C. 247d-7e(c)(5).
Buys development of countermeasures, diagnostics and devices, not enterprise IT.
Organizational placement is in motion: the 2025 reorganization proposed moving ASPR functions to CDC and BARDA to a new office; Congress funded ASPR at $3.7B for FY2026 including $1B for BARDA.

buyers.name: NASA SEWP (vehicle owner)
entry_characteristics: SEWP is the government-wide IT products vehicle DHA, VA and HHS lean on for hardware, software and reseller buys.
SEWP VI awarded 2026-06-22 with 364 initial awardees; ordering opens 2026-11-01; SEWP V extended through 2026-09-30 with options to 2027-04-30 (MMT VA profile, verified 2026-07-09).

buyers.name: State Medicaid agencies (56 jurisdictions)
entry_characteristics: Multi-billion-dollar enterprise systems spend financed at 90 percent federal match for development and 75 percent for operations, inside CMS-approved Advance Planning Documents and Streamlined Modular Certification.
Cooperative purchasing routes: NASPO ValuePoint Cloud and Software Solutions (2026 to 2036, 58 suppliers) through each state's Participating Addendum, and GSA Cooperative Purchasing for MAS IT.
Security programs vary by state: GovRAMP has participating entities in 33 states with formal programs in ten; Texas requires TX-RAMP; MARS-E applies to eligibility systems.
Two dated demand signals: CMS-0057-F APIs due 2027-01-01, and H.R. 1 community engagement requirements by 2026-12-31 with six-month redeterminations for expansion adults.
